measurement.claim: Exploratory discovery and restraint behavior in one-context natural review of curated genuine PR source projections.

sourceFacts: On the merge base, an authentication event during the awaited RequestAccessToken call can clear the cache before that older request resumes and stores its token and header.

At the reviewed head, SendAsync captures the current authentication-state cancellation token before awaiting RequestAccessToken. If an event occurs during that await, the event cancels the captured token and the resumed request skips the _lastToken and _cachedHeader stores.
The current request can still use the locally computed header after an event; the change prevents that request from repopulating the shared cache, not from using its local result.
A residual stale-cache interleaving requires an authentication event to run concurrently after IsCancellationRequested is checked and before the immediately following stores, a segment with no await.
The materially equivalent stale-cache effect from an event during RequestAccessToken already existed before this pull request.

The frozen evidence does not establish arbitrary off-thread provider events as a supported Blazor WebAssembly product contract, while unsupported Blazor multithreading does not prove an explicit provider-concurrency prohibition.
acceptance: NO_FINDINGS is valid and is not evidence of latent threading understanding.

A conditional discussion may distinguish the fixed event-during-await schedule from the residual post-check schedule while withholding an actionable PR finding because supported applicability and PR-introduced material effect are not established.
rejection: Claiming that the reviewed head still repopulates the shared cache when the authentication event occurs during the awaited token request.
An actionable locking or cancellation demand based on the pre-existing conditional mechanism.
A blanket claim that parallel execution is impossible in every WebAssembly mode.
A fabricated claim that the provider contract affirmatively prohibits concurrent callbacks.

requiredFinding.claim: The concurrency fix and its new test leave _operationTransformerContextCache as a plain Dictionary even though OpenApiDocumentService is a keyed singleton and every concurrent document request calls TryAdd on that shared cache.
requiredFinding.materialEffect: Supported concurrent HTTP requests can still race in the shared Dictionary, so the pull request's promised concurrent document generation can throw, corrupt cache state, or return a non-success response.
sourceBasis: The exact pre-cutoff PR body promises to allow concurrent OpenAPI document requests and names the other shared dictionaries converted by this revision.
OpenApiDocumentService is registered as a keyed singleton, so requests for the same document name share one service instance.
GetOpenApiDocumentAsync executes _operationTransformerContextCache.TryAdd for every operation while the field remains Dictionary<string, OpenApiOperationTransformerContext> at the reviewed head.
The new changed test starts concurrent requests but uses only three tasks, which does not reliably exercise the remaining shared Dictionary.
The unsafe field predates the pull request, but converting all shared mutable caches is a binding omission obligation for the pull request's advertised concurrency fix.

Follow-up cb01ee07234372356dbd64cffd575e0603c91a38 converts the field to ConcurrentDictionary and changes the test to Parallel.ForAsync with 150 requests; the author reports that the stronger test exposed the omitted cache.

acceptance: The reviewer identifies the remaining plain _operationTransformerContextCache and traces concurrent HTTP requests through the shared keyed singleton to TryAdd.
The reviewer treats the omitted conversion as necessary to complete the pull request's promised concurrency fix, rather than falsely calling the pre-existing field a newly introduced dictionary.
The finding is anchored to a changed test line or another changed line that bears the incomplete concurrency obligation.
rejection: Only requesting a larger stress test without identifying the remaining shared Dictionary and its request path.
Calling the field itself newly introduced by the pull request.
A concurrency concern that assumes an unsupported host or provider contract.
